help.title: About Inspections
help.overview: An Inspection is a scheduled visit to a unit with a type, status, optional checklist, and findings. It is quality / handover evidence, not a reservation and not a snag list (though findings often become snags). Cancelling a scheduled inspection is a dedicated action; you cannot cancel one that is already completed.

sections.title: What an inspection holds
items: Unit (required), inspector, scheduled date/time, optional checklist template.
Type: initial, follow-up, final, routine, complaint, pre-sale, post-sale.
Status: scheduled → in progress → completed, or cancelled / rescheduled.
Findings grouped by category (structural, electrical, and others) with notes, media, severity (low / medium / high / critical), and optional resolved-at.
Cancellation reason and cancelled-at when you cancel a scheduled visit.

sections.title: Actions
items: Cancel scheduled — only while status is scheduled; stores a reason and timestamp.
Complete the visit by recording findings and moving status to completed (via edit / sheet, depending on access).
Reschedule by setting status to rescheduled and a new date — this is not a new inspection document unless you create one.

sections.title: On this page
items: Create an inspection against a unit. Filter by unit, type, status, date.
Open the sheet to work findings and media.
Company-wide list from the sidebar; from a unit, the list can be scoped.

sections.title: How it behaves
items: An inspection never changes unit commercial status.
It is not a snag: open defects that need a trade and an assignee belong on Snags.
It is not a modification request: client-asked changes go through architect / engineer / CEO / finance / delivery there.
Handover checklists in Configurations can be reused as templates on inspections.

sections.title: Related records
items: Optional checklist template. Follow-on: Snags, Modification requests, Sale handover.
